title: Haaland in the 86th Minute. Norway Break Ivory Coast Hearts in Arlington to Set Up a Date With Brazil.
excerpt: Erling Haaland's fifth goal of the tournament and Antonio Nusa's curling strike send Norway into the Round of 16, where they will face Brazil in New Jersey on Sunday.
body:
The cruelest minutes are always the last ones. Ivory Coast had fought their way back into the game, the Dallas Stadium crowd in Arlington was on its feet, and Amad Diallo's dazzling equaliser in the 74th minute had made the scoreboard read what the match deserved: 1-1. All square. Everything still to play for.

Then Erling Haaland did what Erling Haaland does.

In the 86th minute, substitute Oscar Bobb burst down the right flank and played a pass into the box for Patrick Berg. Berg's cross took a slight deflection, but the ball found its way to Haaland at the far post, who needed only one touch to tap it past Yahia Fofana and send 70,000 people into delirium. Norway 2, Ivory Coast 1. Tournament over for the Elephants. And for the most prolific goalscorer in world football, another chapter written.


![Dallas Stadium — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Arlington_June_2020_4_%28AT%26T_Stadium%29.jpg/3840px-Arlington_June_2020_4_%28AT%26T_Stadium%29.jpg)


## The Goals

Norway's first came in the 39th minute, and it was a beauty. Martin Ødegaard, orchestrating play from deep as only he can, found **Antonio Nusa** on the left wing. The 21-year-old stepped inside onto his right foot and curled a shot into the top corner, arcing it around Fofana's dive with the kind of precision that belies his age. It was the goal of the round so far — a moment of individual brilliance that silenced an Ivory Coast side which had dominated the opening exchanges.



> **"They arrived as reigning Africa Cup of Nations champions, having won the title on home soil in 2024 in one of the most dramatic AFCON campaigns in memory."**


Before Nusa's strike, Ivory Coast had been the better team. Nicolas Pépé was a constant threat down the right, Ghislain Konan dragged a shot into the side-netting from inside the box, and Yan Diomandé picked out Pépé with a searching ball that the Villarreal winger mishit. The African champions were pressing, probing, and creating — they just could not finish.


![Amad Diallo — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/1a/Amad_Diallo_Cote_D%27Ivoire_v_Ecuador_14_June_2026-256_%28cropped_2%29.jpg)


The introduction of **Amad Diallo** on the hour mark changed the game. The Manchester United man had barely been on the pitch for 15 minutes when he picked up the ball wide, danced past two Norwegian defenders, and fired an equaliser that was every bit as brilliant as Nusa's opener. For a brief, electric moment, Ivory Coast believed they could win it.

But Norway had Haaland. And Haaland, as his coach Ståle Solbakken put it afterward, "brings calmness to the team." Even on a day when the Manchester City striker was largely peripheral — one big chance in the first half, long stretches of anonymity in between — he was there when it mattered. The 86th minute. Close range. One touch. Goal. It is his fifth of the tournament, extending a run that now stretches to 13 consecutive competitive international appearances with a goal and 25 goals during that streak.

## What's Next


![Oscar Bobb — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/54/ManCity20240722-050_%28Oscar_Bobb2%29.jpg)


Norway's reward is a Round of 16 date with **Brazil** on Sunday, July 5, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey — a clash that carries the unmistakable scent of a quarterfinal-quality encounter arriving a round too early. Haaland against a Brazilian defence that edged past Japan 2-1 on Monday, courtesy of Gabriel Martinelli's stoppage-time winner. It is the kind of matchup the World Cup was invented for.

For Ivory Coast, the tournament ends with a familiar sting. They arrived as reigning Africa Cup of Nations champions, having won the title on home soil in 2024 in one of the most dramatic AFCON campaigns in memory. But the World Cup has not been kind: a group-stage exit in 2014, a failure to qualify in 2018 and 2022, and now a Round of 32 knockout despite a spirited performance that deserved better.

## The NRI Angle

For Indian fans watching from across the United States, this World Cup continues to deliver spectacle in their backyards. Tuesday's match was at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas — the heart of the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex, home to one of the largest and fastest-growing Indian diaspora communities in the country. The next Norway game will be at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, another epicentre of Indian-American life.

With USA vs Bosnia-Herzegovina in the Round of 32 on Wednesday, and the knockout stage heading to cities like Philadelphia, Houston, and Los Angeles in the coming days, NRI fans have front-row seats to the biggest sporting event on the planet — even if the team they grew up watching plays a different sport entirely.

The Round of 32 continues Wednesday with England vs DR Congo in Atlanta and Belgium vs Senegal in Seattle. The bracket is thinning. The stakes are rising. And Erling Haaland, as ever, is scoring.
